chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated from Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Shashi, who said:

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Katib al-Marwazi said to me: I sent two hundred dinars to Hajiz al-Washsha and wrote to the Gharim (peace be upon him) about it. The reply came, mentioning that he had previously owed me one thousand dinars, and that I had sent him two hundred dinars. He said: 'If you wish to deal with someone, refer to Abu al-Husayn al-Asadi in Ray.' Then news arrived of Hajiz's death after two or three days. I informed him of his death, and he became grieved. I said to him: 'Do not grieve, for in the Tawqi' (letter) addressed to you, there are two indications: one is his informing you that the money owed is one thousand dinars, and the second is his command to you to deal with Abu al-Husayn al-Asadi, knowing the death of Hajiz.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحُسَيْنِ الْأَسَدِيُّ: Abu al-Husayn al-Asadi, a prominent figure in Ray mentioned as a successor or colleague
key_terms.التَّوْقِيعُ: Tawqi', a letter or decree from the Imam
key_terms.الرَّيُّ: Ray, a city near Tehran, Iran
key_terms.الْغَرِيمُ: The Gharim, referring to the Fourth Deputy Muhammad ibn Uthman
key_terms.حَاجِزَ الْوَشَّاءُ: Hajiz al-Washsha, the third of the Four Deputies

ai.seo_question: What signs in the Imam's letter indicated the death of the deputy Hajiz al-Washsha?
ai.summary: This narrative from the Book of Ghayba illustrates the concept of 'Iltifat' (divine attention) in the Fourth Deputy, Hajiz al-Washsha, where the Imam’s Tawqi' contained subtle indicators of his impending death. Specifically, the precise mention of the debt amount and the recommendation of Abu al-Husayn al-Asadi served as signs that the Imam was aware of worldly affairs and had already arranged for administrative continuity. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that the Imam maintains active oversight of the community's affairs even during the Minor Occultation.
